REQ-003.requirement: Every OpenCode V2 feature accounted for

REQ-035.requirement: Preserve safety and resource correctness rather than blindly translate files

localPolicyEvidence.conclusion: Large unrelated contracts must be split; strict RED/GREEN applies to slices; declarative/discovery work still requires executable validators and a failing fixture rather than invented product tests.
RED must compile and execute; declarative/discovery tasks use executable validators plus a captured failing fixture, not fabricated Rust product behavior.
Resource and safety assertions remain deterministic, bounded and fixture-based; no user database mutation or destructive host testing is permitted.

alreadyOwnedRequirementPartitions.disposition: Controller-accepted discovery/source-accounting owners exist; REL-001 has no separate behavior surface or source contract that creates a native product module.
Strict-TDD workflow is already defined by repository policy and automation ownership; frozen AUTO-005 is not reopened through REL-002.
Safety/resource-correctness policy is shared; the two residual REL ids are not distinguishable by source, surface, task card or requirement wording.

candidateValidatorContracts.inputs: canonical plan, requirements, source reconciliation, backlog exhaustion ledger and controller statuses
candidateValidatorContracts.outputs: machine-verifiable proof that every required feature is accounted for without converting local evidence into controller acceptance
candidateValidatorContracts.failureSemantics: nonzero validation with a concrete missing/misclassified feature fixture
candidateValidatorContracts.resourceLifetime: bounded local files and deterministic validator execution
disqualifiers: REL-001 has no task card or direct validator contract.
DISC-001/DISC-010 already own source-accounting requirements and current validators cover substantial portions of the same assurance space.
A new REL validator must be source-grounded and must not duplicate an existing check solely to make the numeric task appear implemented.

candidateValidatorContracts.inputs: frozen test manifests, independent verification results, security/resource gates and release candidate revision
candidateValidatorContracts.outputs: deterministic pass/fail release assurance with attributable failing fixture
candidateValidatorContracts.failureSemantics: nonzero validation on missing RED/GREEN proof, mutable frozen evidence, unsafe resource behavior or unverified release state
candidateValidatorContracts.stateLifetime: one exact candidate revision and its immutable evidence set
candidateValidatorContracts.resourceLifetime: bounded validator/test execution with no host-destructive or user-DB mutation
disqualifiers: REL-002 and REL-003 share REQ-035 and have no source/surface distinction.
REQ-004 also overlaps accepted AUTO-002 and frozen AUTO-005, so residual arithmetic cannot identify REL-002 semantics.
Repository policy requires a failing executable validator fixture before declarative assurance can be claimed.

closureCriteria: Do not create a Rust product module for REL-001/002/003 unless new source-grounded product semantics and ownership appear; current rows are release/declarative assurance only.

Each REL ownership change requires an explicit task-specific declarative validator contract, executable failing fixture, expected outputs/failures and exact evidence lifetime rather than requirement subtraction or task-number inference.
Existing DISC/AUTO/SEC ownership and frozen blockers remain excluded; a new validator must add a distinct release guarantee instead of duplicating an already enforced invariant.

The three required declarative partitions must be assigned by explicit task evidence or remain unresolved; empty behavior-surface membership is not proof that any particular validator belongs to a REL id.
